company.name: Exa
company.one_liner: Search API for AI agents that need real-time web data.

summary.text: Exa grows as a developer platform. A free API tier, an MCP server and SDKs get developers building, and it rides other platforms people already use: Vercel, Codex, ChatGPT and Firefox. It ships something every week or two and announces each launch on X and LinkedIn, where the CEO's posts draw the biggest numbers. Search ads and comparison pages catch people already shopping for a search API.

channels.read: The CEO's X posts get the biggest numbers of any account we sampled; his $100m revenue post drew about 40 times his usual engagement.
channels.activity: X: 9 posts in 2 weeks sampled · LinkedIn: 11.5k followers

channels.read: 50 public repos with 8,545 stars. The MCP server and two demo apps built on the API carry most of them.
channels.activity: 4 of the top repos pushed this month

channels.read: Three platform launches in two months put Exa inside tools developers already use: Vercel, Codex and ChatGPT, and Firefox.
The company announces launches as X threads and LinkedIn posts every few days. The Exa 3.0 launch thread drew about 35 times the account's usual engagement on X.
A steady search-ad program: 22 ads running now, all started in October, replacing ads that ran for most of a year.
10 "versus" and 9 "alternatives" pages, with every alternatives page refreshed in the last 90 days.
A docs-heavy site: 163 docs pages, 68 blog pages and a data library. Half the blog was updated in the last 90 days.
One button on the homepage, "Try API for free", straight into the dashboard with $10 of free credits a month.
Four webinars and meetups since mid-August, three of them between 30 Sep and 15 Oct, mostly co-hosted with another company (Crunchbase, Aaru, Gemini).
A 5,115-member Discord; Hacker News attention is modest.
An llms.txt and open access for every AI crawler.
At least one launch post was promoted as a paid LinkedIn post.

connections.text: Launches travel through every owned channel at once: an X thread, a LinkedIn post, a blog post and, for the biggest launch, a paid LinkedIn boost.

notable_plays.text: Open-source demo apps double as marketing: a company-research tool and a DeepSeek chat app built on the API have 1,517 and 728 stars.
The site identifies who visits: RB2B and Common Room name visiting companies, Default routes inbound leads, and Tolt runs an affiliate program.
Search ads go after buyers outside the core developer audience too, such as people searching for a people or phone-number lookup API.
